. Like other event maps, this map had a specialized wave structure with special enemies. Players started with a varying amount of cash, based on how many players there are in the match. The rewards received were based on how many waves were survived and if the match was won. This map had two difficulties, Easy and Hard.

Cash was only gained if an enemy is killed, or in some cases, damaged by a specific amount of health. Additionally, the amount gained was a set amount of cash, which was not always equal to the enemy's health. Enemies split their cash between players, regardless of how much damage the player dealt to it. If, in a duo, one player did all the damage to an enemy, both players would receive 50% of the cash the enemy would normally give in solo. This meant that in solo, you received 100% of the cash when an enemy was killed, or it was damaged enough. With each additional player, this is reduced to 50% in duo, 33% in trio and 25% in quad. If it is a decimal, it gets rounded up or down depending on the decimal value. If it is at least 0.5, it gets rounded up. If it is less than 0.5, it gets rounded down.
Health of enemies in this mode scaled with player count and difficulty.
In Easy, the increase was 5% in duo, 20% in trio and 40% in quad.
In Hard, the increase was 30% in duo, 60% in trio and 70% in quad.

The map itself went through multiple changes as the waves progress. The

fragments initially laid on the floor and did not start to merge until later. The map started out with an orange sky, which became darker after the first cutscene. The whole outpost also broke apart as waves go on, with some buildings getting completely destroyed.
Three paths started at separate portals, converging very early on and taking a few 90-degree turns before ending at a gate leading to the inside of the research base.

Urgh! This should work! Maybe if we had the shards from the Children of Exo it'd be more stable!
It's too late to stop the merging process, but it should be possible to stabilize it. We just need more time.
Don't worry, we've got you. Commander, focus on organizing the units and protecting the control station. Nothing gets by us.
I can't believe what I'm seeing. These readings suggest that the shards aren't the corruption itself, but instead the container that prevents it from escaping.
The power inside these shards are condensing as they merge, their physical state is weak enough to allow that energy out.
If this continues, it will corrupt the space around it and tear apart our reality. We can't contain something this powerful!
This is bigger than we thought...
I knew it! There had to be something out there! I theorized that if portals act as tunnels to other realms, then what kind of space were we tunneling through?
We've named that space the 'Nil Zone'. I never thought a place like that could exist.
What are you trying to say?
There could be things stronger than anything we've seen before. It's not a question of what's out there, but who.
What just happened?! It looks like we've been hit with a curse!
Be careful! Anything could happen while our realm destabilizes!
Hey, uhh... Can we talk about why those things look like us?
Those Nil Zone creatures may be more sensitive to the corruption than we are. As the energy expands outwards, it might be violently ripping through your bodies and replicating your DNA into them!
Are we--are we are we going to be alright?!
You know, I kind of miss being out in the field. Reminds me of our earlier years.
Is that Freezer?! Look what's happened to him!
Watch out! He's firing at us!
Those creatures are coming through the rifts!
ARGH! These guys aren't giving up! V, how much longer?
